L: The flight to San Antonio leaves at fourteen fifteen, not at four fifteen.
o: At 2:15 in the afternoon
At 4:15 in the afternoon
At 4:50 in the morning
At 2:50 in the afternoon
items.e: In military time, fourteen fifteen (1415) is 2:15 p.m. The speaker corrects the mistake "four fifteen".

L: Can I give you a hand with those boxes?
o: Thanks, that would be great.
Yes, I have two hands.
They are in the boxes.
I gave it to him yesterday.
items.e: "Give someone a hand" means help them. The best answer accepts the help.

L: Do you know what time the dining facility opens?
o: At six thirty, I think.
Yes, the food is very good.
I ate there yesterday.
It's next to the gym.
items.e: The question asks for a time, so the best answer gives one.

L: I've been waiting for over an hour, and the mechanic still hasn't called me.
items.q: How does the man probably feel?
o: Impatient
Relaxed
Grateful
Sleepy
items.e: Waiting more than an hour with no news makes a person impatient.

o: The movie was boring.
The movie was exciting.
She did not go to the movie.
She saw the movie twice.
items.e: She fell asleep in the middle of the movie: she suggests that it was boring.

L: I get thirty days of leave a year, and so far I've taken ten in June and eight in August.
items.q: How many days of leave does the speaker have left this year?
o: Twelve
Eighteen
Twenty
Thirty
items.e: He has taken 10 + 8 = 18 days. "Thirty days" minus 18 days leaves 12 days.

L: The tires we ordered were delivered on Monday, the day before yesterday.
o: Wednesday
Tuesday
Monday
Saturday
items.e: "The day before yesterday" was Monday, so yesterday was Tuesday. Today is Wednesday.

L: How much do I owe you for the coffee and the muffin?
o: The man does not have to pay.
The man can pay her tomorrow.
The food was made at her house.
The coffee costs more today.
items.e: "On the house" means free, paid for by the business. The man does not have to pay.

L: What did you get on the listening test?
o: I got an eighty-five.
I got it at the bookstore.
I got there at eight.
I took it on Monday.
items.e: "What did you get on the listening test?" asks about the score. "An eighty-five" is a score.

L: Could you repeat the last question, please?
o: Of course. I'll read it again.
Yes, it was the last one.
I answered it last week.
It was a hard question.
items.e: "Could you repeat...?" is a polite request. "Of course. I'll read it again" agrees to do it.

L: Sorry, I have another call coming in. Can we finish this conversation later?
No problem. Let's touch base tomorrow morning.
o: They should talk again tomorrow morning.
They should go to the base together tomorrow.
She should not answer the other call.
He should call her back in a few minutes.
items.e: "Let's touch base tomorrow morning" means "let's contact each other again tomorrow morning". It has nothing to do with a military base.

L: The barracks inspection got moved up to Wednesday.
Wednesday? I was counting on the weekend to get my wall locker squared away.
o: She has less time to prepare than planned.
She will be away on the day of the inspection.
She doesn't know where her wall locker is.
She thought the inspection had been canceled.
items.e: "Moved up" means earlier, so she loses the weekend she had planned to use to prepare.

L: Did you enjoy the trip to the mountains?
It was out of this world.
o: It was wonderful.
It was very far away.
It was boring.
She didn't go.
items.e: "Out of this world" means excellent.

L: Did you buy the blue shirt or the white one?
I couldn't make up my mind, so I got both.
o: He bought two shirts.
He bought only the blue one.
He bought nothing.
He returned both shirts.
items.e: He couldn't decide, so he bought both.

L: Did you send the training schedule to the battalion yet?
It's ready to go, but the operations officer asked for one more change before it goes out.
items.q: Why hasn't the schedule been sent?
o: It still needs to be revised.
The battalion already has a copy.
The operations officer lost it.
Nobody has typed it up yet.
items.e: The operations officer wants another change made before it is sent.

L: Has finance paid you for your trip to the conference yet?
No, they sent my travel voucher back twice for missing receipts.

o: His paperwork was incomplete.
He never went to the conference.
Finance lost his receipts twice.
He forgot to send his voucher.
items.e: His claim was returned because some receipts were not included.

L: My car won't start this morning.
Let me get the jumper cables from my trunk.

o: Help start his car
Call a taxi
Drive him to work
Buy a new battery

Go to the personnel office in Building Three.

o: Where to get an ID card
When the office opens
How much the card costs
Who signs the card

L: I've been coughing for a week.
Take this syrup twice a day and come back if it doesn't help.
o: A doctor
A cook
A teacher
A store clerk
items.e: She gives medical instructions.

L: Sorry, I don't have that much in the register.
o: A cashier
A bus driver
A police officer
A banker

Confirm the Tuesday appointment.
Go to the dental clinic early.
Cancel her day at the range.

One large pizza
One medium pizza
No pizza

She agrees completely.
She disagrees completely.

items.e: She supports the principle only.

Try the front desk. Whoever used the room last was supposed to drop it off there.

Moving the meeting to another room.
Starting the meeting five minutes late.
Calling the last person who used the room.

Sergeant Lopez approved it.
It will not change.

Get a new one from the operations office.

Using the old map
Asking a local
Drawing a map

I can't lift that box by myself.

It is now on Tuesday.
items.e: The office moved it from Monday to Wednesday, two days later.

L: My brother lives in Texas, and my sister lives two hours away from him.
o: Two hours from her brother
Two hours from the speaker
In a different country
In the same house as her brother
items.e: Her sister is two hours from the brother in Texas.

L: The shoe store is closing, so everything is seventy percent off.
o: The store is going out of business.
The shoes are damaged.
It is the end of summer.
The store just opened.
items.e: A closing sale lowers prices.

L: I've lived in this town for five years, but I still get lost downtown.
items.q: What is true about the speaker?
o: He still gets lost downtown.
He just moved to town.
He knows downtown very well.
He never goes downtown.
items.e: Even after five years he gets lost.

L: My roommate and I split the rent, so each of us pays four hundred dollars.
items.q: How much is the total rent?
items.e: Two people paying $400 each make $800.

L: The hardware store gave me the wrong size of screws, so I have to go back.
items.q: Why does he have to go back?
o: He got the wrong screws.
He forgot his receipt.
The store called him.
He needs more paint.
items.e: The screws were the wrong size.

L: My favorite store moved from the mall to a building downtown.
items.q: What does the woman say about her favorite store?
o: It is now in the center of town.
It moved from downtown into the mall.
It opened a second branch at the mall.
It closed its building downtown.
items.e: The store left the mall for a building downtown, so it is now in the center of town.

L: My father taught me to fish when I was six years old.
items.q: When did he learn to fish?
o: At age six
At age sixteen
Last year
When he joined the army
items.e: His father taught him at six.

L: The library is on the second floor of the education center, above the bookstore.
items.q: What can be concluded about the bookstore?
o: It is on a lower floor than the library.
It is on the second floor with the library.
It is in a separate building nearby.
It is on the floor above the library.
items.e: The library is above the bookstore, so the bookstore is on a lower floor.

L: The new students will be divided into four groups of fifteen.
items.q: How many new students are there?
o: Sixty
Fifteen
Forty
Nineteen
items.e: Four groups of fifteen is sixty.

L: The pilot trainees must log forty hours of flight time before their solo flight.
items.q: What is true about the pilot trainees?
o: They need 40 hours before flying alone.
They must fly alone for forty hours.
They will fly solo on their first day.
They need fourteen hours in the air first.
items.e: Their solo flight comes only after they log forty hours of flight time.

L: My roommate studies at night, but I prefer to study early in the morning.
items.q: What is the difference between the man and his roommate?
o: Their study schedules are not the same.
The roommate studies early in the morning.
They study together late every night.
The man studies longer than his roommate.
items.e: The roommate studies at night and the man studies in the morning, so their schedules differ.

L: The lecture on safety will be repeated next week for those who missed it.
items.q: Why will the lecture be repeated?
o: Some people missed it.
It was too difficult.
The speaker was late.
It was canceled.
items.e: It is repeated for those who missed it.

L: Lieutenant Park is always on the ball; she had the reports finished before the rest of us even started.
items.q: What does the man say about Lieutenant Park?
o: She is quick and well organized.
She likes to play ball with the team.
She started the reports late.
She finished last as usual.
items.e: "On the ball" means alert and efficient; she finished before the others began.

L: I passed the driving test by the skin of my teeth.
o: She barely passed.
She got a perfect score.
She failed the test.
She went to the dentist.
items.e: "By the skin of my teeth" means just barely.

L: My hands are shaking, and I can't eat a thing; my promotion board starts in less than an hour.
o: Anxious about an upcoming event
Hungry but too busy to eat
Bored with waiting for a meeting
Angry about a missed promotion
items.e: Shaking hands and no appetite before an important board show that he is nervous.

L: We've got our work cut out for us; the inspection is Monday, and half the vehicles still need new tires.
o: They have a hard job ahead.
The inspection has been canceled.
Their workload has been reduced.
Monday is a day off for the unit.
items.e: "Have your work cut out for you" means facing a difficult job.

L: I'd have finished the report by now if the printer hadn't jammed every few pages.
o: The report is not done yet.
The report was finished early.
The printer worked perfectly.
She printed only a few pages.
items.e: The conditional shows that the jammed printer has kept her from finishing.

L: The mechanic says it will be cheaper to fix the old car than to buy a new one.
o: Repair is cheaper.
A new car would cost about the same
The old car can't be fixed at all
Buying a used car is the best choice
items.e: Fixing costs less than replacing.

L: Most of the snow melted yesterday, but the roads are still slippery.
o: Drivers should still be careful.
The roads are covered with deep snow.
More snow is expected tomorrow.
The roads are dry and safe again.
items.e: The snow has mostly melted, but slippery roads mean drivers still need to be careful.

L: The convenience store is open twenty-four hours, but the pharmacy inside closes at nine.
o: The pharmacy section has shorter hours.
The whole store closes at nine every night.
The pharmacy stays open around the clock.
The pharmacy is in a separate building nearby.
items.e: The store never closes, but the pharmacy closes at nine, so the pharmacy has shorter hours.

L: The judge gave the driver a fine instead of sending him to jail.
o: He avoided prison but had to pay money.
He paid a fine and then went to jail.
He was sent to jail for a short time.
He was found not guilty by the judge.
items.e: A fine instead of jail means he paid money but was not locked up.

L: Our gym has forty treadmills, but a quarter of them are broken, so there's usually a line in the evening.
o: Thirty
Forty
Ten
Twenty-five
items.e: A quarter of forty is ten, so thirty treadmills still work.

L: You need a reservation to eat at that restaurant on Fridays.
items.q: What should someone do before going to the restaurant on a Friday?
o: Book a table in advance.
Arrive early to get a seat.
Pay for the meal ahead of time.
Eat somewhere else; it is closed.
items.e: A reservation is required on Fridays, so you must book a table ahead.

L: The tour bus stops at five famous places in the city.
o: A sightseeing trip with several stops
A bus that leaves five times every day
A city that has five famous bus stations
A tour of five nearby cities
items.e: A tour bus that stops at five famous places is a sightseeing trip.

L: The bank will charge a fee if your balance goes below a hundred dollars.
items.q: When will the bank charge a fee?
o: If the balance is under $100
If the balance is over $100
Every month
Never
items.e: A low balance triggers the fee.

L: I've decided to take guitar lessons. Do you think I'm too old to start?
Not at all. My uncle learned to play at sixty, and now he performs at weddings.
o: Encouraging
Doubtful
Impatient
Uninterested
items.e: She says he is not too old and gives the example of her uncle, so she encourages him.

L: I need proof that this letter was delivered. Is there a way to do that?
Send it certified. The person has to sign for it, and you'll get a receipt online.
items.q: What is the man concerned about?
o: Confirming that his mail arrives
Paying too much for postage
Losing his receipt online
Getting a signature from his boss
items.e: He wants proof of delivery, that is, confirmation that the letter arrived.

L: Your tomatoes look great this year. What's your secret?
No secret, really. I just water them early every morning before it gets hot.
o: Her method is a simple one.
She will not share her secret.
She waters the plants at night.
The tomatoes need more sunlight.
items.e: She says there is no secret; she only waters the tomatoes early each morning.

L: I'd like to return this jacket. I don't have the receipt, though.
In that case, I can only give you store credit, not cash.
items.q: What does the woman tell the man?
o: He cannot get his money back.
He must find the receipt first.
He can pay with a credit card.
The jacket cannot be returned.
items.e: Without a receipt he will receive store credit instead of a cash refund.

L: When did you last have the oil changed in this car?
To be honest, I can't remember. It's been at least a year, maybe longer.
o: The car is overdue for service.
The oil was changed last week.
She changed the oil herself.
She bought the car a year ago.
items.e: More than a year without an oil change means maintenance is overdue.

L: Does this dress come in a smaller size?
Not in blue, I'm afraid. We've got your size in black, though, if you'd like to try it on.
o: Another color in her size
The blue dress in a smaller size
A discount on the blue dress
A larger size in a darker color
items.e: Her size is available only in black, not in blue.

L: I heard your sister just had a baby. Boy or girl?
Twins, actually! One of each, so now I have a niece and a nephew.
items.q: What does the woman say about her sister?
o: She had a son and a daughter.
She had two baby boys at once.
She had two baby girls.
She is expecting a baby soon.
items.e: Twins, "one of each," means one boy and one girl.

L: How often do your kids get to see their grandparents?
o: Only during summer vacation, sadly.
They're seventy and seventy-two.
My kids are both in fourth grade.
Their grandparents live in Maine.
items.e: "How often" asks about frequency, and the reply says only once a year in summer.

L: I'm afraid you've dialed the wrong number. Nobody named Kevin lives here.
o: Oh, sorry to have bothered you.
He's lived here for about a year.
Nobody told me about it either.
I'm afraid I can't make it tonight.
items.e: A caller who reached the wrong house naturally apologizes.

L: The colonel said that leave requests for December must be turned in by November fifteenth.
items.q: When are December leave requests due?
o: By November 15
By December 15
By November 1
By December 1
items.e: The deadline is November fifteenth.

L: Anyone pulling guard tonight is excused from the morning run, but they still have to make the noon formation.
items.q: What is true about the soldiers on guard tonight?
o: They must be at the midday formation.
They must run in the morning.
They are excused from all formations.
They will guard the gate again at noon.
items.e: They skip the morning run, but they still have to attend the formation at noon.

L: Leave requests for the holidays must reach the orderly room no later than the fifteenth, or they won't be considered.
o: Late requests will be rejected.
Leave begins on the fifteenth.
The orderly room closes for the holidays.
Requests are handled in the order received.
items.e: Requests that arrive after the fifteenth will not be considered.

L: If you lose your ID card, report it to the military police before you go to get a replacement.
items.q: What should be done first after losing an ID card?
o: Notify the MPs about the loss.
Request a new card right away.
Ask a friend to help search for it.
Pay a fine at the ID card office.
items.e: The military police (MPs) must be told before a replacement card is requested.

L: We'll march to the ceremony site in formation, but buses will bring everyone back afterward.
items.q: How will the soldiers return from the ceremony?
o: They will be driven.
They will march back.
They will drive their own cars.
They will run back in formation.
items.e: Buses will take everyone back, so they will ride, not march.

L: The lieutenant wasn't happy that only half the platoon had their reflective belts on during this morning's run.
o: Many soldiers lacked required safety gear.
Half the platoon didn't show up for the run.
The run started late this morning.
Soldiers wore the wrong belts to work.
items.e: Half the platoon ran without their reflective belts, which are safety equipment.

L: Soldiers who haven't qualified on their weapons this year won't be allowed to deploy, so the range is open again Saturday.
items.q: Why is the range open again on Saturday?
o: Not everyone has met the shooting standard.
Saturday is the only day without other training.
Soldiers are deploying this weekend.
The range was closed earlier this year.
items.e: Some soldiers have not qualified yet, and they must do so before they can deploy.

L: Specialists aren't noncommissioned officers, so even though Specialist Hall has more time in service, Corporal Reyes is in charge of the team.
items.q: Why is Corporal Reyes leading the team?
o: Reyes's rank comes with more authority.
Reyes has served longer than Hall.
Hall asked Reyes to take over.
Reyes is a commissioned officer.
items.e: A corporal is an NCO and a specialist is not, so Reyes leads even though Hall has served longer.

L: Commander's call has been rescheduled for Thursday at fifteen hundred, and attendance is mandatory for everyone except those on guard.
items.q: Who does not have to attend the meeting?
o: Soldiers on security duty.
Soldiers who have a call to make.
Anyone who is busy at three o'clock.
The commander and his staff.
items.e: Everyone must attend except the soldiers pulling guard.

L: Since the staff duty runner may not leave the desk, he'll need someone to bring his dinner from the dining facility.
items.q: Why can't the runner get his own dinner?
o: He has to stay at his post.
The dining facility has closed.
He is not allowed to eat on duty.
Someone else is using his desk.
items.e: The runner is not permitted to leave the desk, so someone must bring him food.

L: Before you take the truck out of the motor pool, check the oil and tire pressure and sign the dispatch log.
o: Giving instructions to a driver
Reporting a problem with a tire
Asking for help with the oil
Explaining why a vehicle is late
items.e: He is telling a driver the steps to follow before leaving with the truck.

L: The rental company charges drivers under twenty-five an extra fee, so my son can't afford to rent a car for the trip.
items.q: Why won't the woman's son rent a car?
o: He is too young to get the regular price.
He does not have a driver's license.
The rental company has no cars available.
He is going to travel with his mother.
items.e: Drivers under twenty-five pay an extra fee, and her son cannot afford it.

L: This envelope needs extra postage because it's thicker than a quarter of an inch, even though it's light.
items.q: Why does the envelope cost more to mail?
o: Its size, not its weight, is the problem.
It weighs more than a quarter of a pound.
It is going to another country.
It needs to arrive by tomorrow.
items.e: The envelope is light but too thick, so the extra cost is because of its size.

L: The agent moved me to first class because my original seat was broken, and she didn't charge me a cent.
o: She got a better seat for free.
She paid extra to change seats.
She had to sit in a broken seat.
She was moved to a later flight.
items.e: She was moved to first class at no cost because her seat was broken.

L: I filled up the tank before returning the car, but they still charged me because the gauge wasn't quite on full.
o: The car needed a bit more gas.
He returned the car late.
He forgot to fill up the tank.
The fuel gauge was broken.
items.e: The gauge was not completely on full, so the company charged him for the missing fuel.

L: The airport is only twelve miles away, but you should allow an hour, since the road out there is always backed up.
items.q: Why does the woman suggest leaving early?
o: Traffic on the way is usually heavy.
The airport is very far away.
The road is closed for an hour.
Check-in takes about an hour.
items.e: "Backed up" means the road is full of slow traffic.

L: Military members can check two bags for free on most airlines when they're traveling on orders.
items.q: When is there no charge for two bags?
o: When a soldier is on duty travel
When the soldier flies on a military plane
When the bags weigh less than two pounds
When the soldier pays for the ticket
items.e: "Traveling on orders" means official travel for duty.

L: I'll drop you off at departures, park the car in the long-term lot, and meet you at the check-in counter.
items.q: What will the woman do after dropping the man off?
o: Leave the car and join him inside
Drive straight back home
Pick him up at arrivals
Wait for him in the parking lot
items.e: She will park and then meet him at the check-in counter.

L: You can't drive through the gate without a base sticker, so visitors have to get a pass at the visitor center first.
items.q: What must a guest do before entering the base?
o: Stop at a building to get permission
Buy a sticker at the gate
Drive through the gate slowly
Call the base to get a sticker
items.e: Visitors need a pass from the visitor center before driving in.

L: While the dining facility is closed for renovations next week, hot meals will be served out of the gym instead.
items.q: Why will meals be served in a different place next week?
o: The usual building is being remodeled.
The gym is closed for repairs.
The cooks will be out in the field.
Too many soldiers eat there now.
items.e: The dining facility is closed for renovations, which means it is being remodeled.

L: My flu shot is due, but the clinic's walk-in hours conflict with my shift, so I'll have to make an appointment.
items.q: Why can't the man just walk in to get his flu shot?
o: He is on duty during those hours.
The clinic has run out of flu vaccine.
He has already had one this year.
The clinic only takes walk-ins on weekends.
items.e: The walk-in hours conflict with his shift, so he is working at those times.

L: Coach says anyone who misses two practices in a row won't start in Saturday's game, no matter how good they are.
o: Players who miss consecutive practices won't start.
The best players can skip practice before a game.
Everyone must practice twice before Saturday's game.
Players who are not good enough won't play Saturday.
items.e: Missing two practices in a row means a player will not start the game.

L: For a sprained ankle, rest it, put ice on it for twenty minutes at a time, and keep it raised above your heart.
items.q: Which of the following does the man recommend?
o: Keeping the injured leg elevated.
Walking on the ankle to keep it loose.
Keeping ice on it for an hour.
Wrapping the ankle in a warm towel.
items.e: Keeping the ankle raised above the heart means elevating it.

L: If you're driving on post after dark, slow down near the housing area; kids are out trick-or-treating until eight tonight.
items.q: Why should drivers be extra careful tonight?
o: Lots of children will be walking around.
The roads in the housing area are dark.
There is construction near the housing area.
The speed limit changes at eight o'clock.
items.e: Kids will be out trick-or-treating, so many children will be walking around.

L: The pollen count is at a record high today, so if you have allergies, keep your windows closed and shower after training outside.
items.q: Who is the man's advice mainly for?
o: People who react to pollen.
People who train indoors.
People who just moved here.
People who need to count supplies.
items.e: The advice is for anyone with allergies, meaning those who react to pollen.

L: They've started weighing the food we throw away at the dining facility, and the unit that wastes the least wins a pizza party.
items.q: What is the purpose of the program?
o: To reduce how much food is wasted.
To find out which unit eats the most.
To raise money for a pizza party.
To reduce the weight of the soldiers.
items.e: Rewarding the unit that wastes the least encourages everyone to waste less.

L: I was going to give blood today, but they turned me away because I'd just gotten back from a country with malaria.
items.q: Why couldn't the man donate blood?
o: His recent trip disqualified him.
He had come down with malaria.
He was too tired from his trip.
The blood drive was canceled today.
items.e: He was turned away because he had recently been in a country with malaria.

L: The obstacle course is off-limits until the engineers repair the rope bridge, so we'll run hill sprints this afternoon instead.
items.q: Why has the afternoon training been changed?
o: Part of the course needs fixing.
The engineers are using the hill.
The rope bridge is too crowded.
It is too hot for hill sprints.
items.e: The rope bridge on the obstacle course needs repairs, so the course can't be used.

L: I scored a sixty-eight on the practice test, and I need at least seventy-five to qualify for the advanced course.
items.q: What can be concluded about the man?
o: He has not yet reached the required score.
He has already qualified for the advanced course.
He needs to raise his score by about five points.
He scored seventy-five on the practice test.
items.e: He got 68 but needs 75, so his score is still too low (he needs seven more points).

L: You may use a dictionary on the reading section, but not on the listening section, and phones must stay in your bag.
items.q: What are students allowed to do?
o: Check word meanings during part of the test
Use a dictionary for every section of the test
Keep their phones on their desks
Look up words during the listening section
items.e: A dictionary is allowed only in the reading section, which is one part of the test.

L: The supply room is locked after five, so if you need paper or toner, get it from Mrs. Chen before she leaves.
items.q: What should people do if they need supplies?
o: Pick them up before the end of the day
Ask Mrs. Chen for the key after five
Order paper and toner online
Wait until the supply room opens at five
items.e: The room is locked after five, so supplies must be picked up from Mrs. Chen before she goes home.

L: If the director doesn't sign the purchase request by Friday, we'll have to wait until next quarter to buy new desks.
items.q: What will happen if the request isn't signed by Friday?
o: The new furniture will be delayed.
The director will order the desks himself.
The desks will be delivered on Friday.
The office will get used desks instead.
items.e: Without the signature, the desks cannot be bought until next quarter.

L: The new software is supposed to save us time, but so far it's taken me twice as long to enter each order.
items.q: What does the man say about the new software?
o: It has slowed him down so far.
It has cut his work time in half.
It saves time on each order.
It was installed twice by mistake.
items.e: Each order now takes him twice as long, so the software has made him slower.

L: The new laptops won't arrive until March, so the old ones will have to last another three months.
o: The current computers will be kept for now.
The new laptops have already been delivered.
The old laptops broke three months ago.
The new laptops will last three months.
items.e: Until the new laptops come in March, people will keep using the old ones.

L: I don't have much signal out here at the range, so text me instead of calling if it's urgent.
items.q: Why does the man prefer text messages?
o: Phone reception is weak where he is.
He is too busy to talk while he is at the range.
Calls are not allowed at the range.
His phone cannot make calls.
items.e: He has a poor signal at the range, and a text can get through when a call might not.

L: I hardly ever check my voicemail, so if you need me, send a text and I'll get back to you right away.
o: Reaching her by text message is best.
She checks her voicemail every hour.
She'll call back after work.
Leave her a detailed voicemail message.
items.e: She rarely checks voicemail but answers texts quickly.

L: Our quarterly meeting used to last all morning, but the new director cut it down to forty-five minutes.
items.q: What has changed about the quarterly meeting?
o: It is much shorter now.
It is held in the afternoon.
It lasts all morning now.
It has a new location.
items.e: "Used to last all morning" but now it takes only forty-five minutes.

L: The jacket was forty dollars off, but the sale ended before I reached the register, so I left it there.
items.q: Why didn't the woman buy the jacket?
o: The discount was no longer available.
The jacket cost forty dollars too much.
The register was closed when she arrived.
She found a cheaper one somewhere else.
items.e: The sale ended before she paid, so the lower price was gone and she did not buy it.

L: The heater in the basement hardly works anymore, so we're replacing it before the cold weather sets in.
items.q: Why is the heater being replaced?
o: It has almost stopped working.
It is too big for the basement.
It broke during the cold weather.
It works too hard and wastes energy.
items.e: "Hardly works" means it almost does not work, so they are replacing it before winter.

L: I'm not flying home for the holidays this year because ticket prices nearly doubled, so I'll visit my family in February instead.
items.q: Why isn't the woman traveling for the holidays?
o: Airfare is too expensive right now.
Her family is coming to visit her instead.
She has to work in February.
Her flight was canceled twice.
items.e: Plane tickets almost doubled in price, so she will wait and visit in February.

L: The used car looks great, but I won't buy it until my mechanic has had a chance to look under the hood.
items.q: What will the man do before deciding?
o: Have the car inspected.
Buy it right away.
Ask for a lower price.
Test-drive a different car.
items.e: He wants his mechanic to check the engine before he makes a decision.

L: The salesman kept pushing the extended warranty, but the laptop already comes with two years of coverage, so I said no.
items.q: Why did the woman turn down the warranty?
o: She saw no need for extra protection.
She thought the salesman was rude to her.
The warranty lasted only two years.
She couldn't afford the laptop and the plan.
items.e: The laptop is already covered for two years, so she decided the extra warranty was not needed.

L: We got three estimates for the new fence, and even the cheapest one was fifteen hundred dollars more than we'd budgeted.
o: Every offer is higher than they planned for.
They chose the most expensive estimate.
The fence cost fifteen hundred dollars.
Only one contractor gave them an estimate.
items.e: Even the lowest estimate was $1,500 above their budget, so every estimate costs more than they planned.

L: My in-laws are staying with us for two weeks, so we're giving them our bedroom and sleeping on the couch ourselves.
items.q: Where will the woman sleep for the next two weeks?
o: In the living room.
In the guest room.
In her own bedroom.
At her in-laws' house.
items.e: Her guests get her bedroom, so she will sleep on the couch, which is in the living room.

L: The turkey needs about four hours in the oven, so if we want to eat at six, it has to go in by two.
items.q: When must the turkey start cooking?
o: No later than two o'clock.
No later than four o'clock.
No earlier than six o'clock.
No later than ten o'clock.
items.e: Four hours before six o'clock is two o'clock, so it must be in the oven by then.

L: Our cat kept scratching the couch until we bought her a scratching post, and now she leaves the furniture alone.
o: Giving the cat something else to claw.
Buying a new couch for the living room.
Keeping the cat out of the house.
Trimming the cat's claws every week.
items.e: Once the cat had a post to scratch, she stopped damaging the couch.

L: The neighbors are having a yard sale this Saturday, so expect cars parked up and down our street all morning.
items.q: What is the man warning about?
o: Lots of visitors' cars nearby that day.
A car sale on their street on Saturday.
Road repairs planned for the morning.
Their own yard sale this weekend.
items.e: Many shoppers will come to the yard sale, so the street will be full of parked cars.

L: The PX doesn't open until ten on Sundays, so if you need boot polish for Sunday's nine o'clock formation, buy it today.
o: Buying the polish ahead of time.
Going to the PX at nine on Sunday.
Skipping formation to go shopping.
Waiting until ten to buy the polish.
items.e: The store opens after the formation on Sunday, so the polish must be bought the day before.

L: I drove the forty miles to the depot in under an hour, but coming back in heavy traffic took nearly two.
items.q: What does the man say about the return trip?
o: It took about twice as long.
It was forty miles longer.
It was faster than the trip there.
It took less than an hour.
items.e: Under an hour going and nearly two hours coming back means the return took about twice as long.

L: My platoon finished the ruck march in second place, just three minutes behind first and well ahead of the other five platoons.
items.q: What can be concluded about the woman's platoon?
o: Only one platoon beat hers.
Her platoon came in last.
Her platoon won by three minutes.
Five platoons finished ahead of hers.
items.e: Second place means exactly one platoon finished ahead of hers.

L: As soon as the last pallet is on the truck, call the dispatcher; she won't send a driver until she hears from you.
items.q: What must happen before a driver is sent?
o: Someone must phone the dispatcher.
The driver must call the man.
The pallets must be counted.
The truck needs to be refueled.
items.e: The dispatcher waits for a call before she sends a driver.

L: Everything in the store is twenty-five percent off today, and members get an extra ten dollars off any purchase over fifty.
items.q: How much would a member pay for an item marked forty dollars?
o: Thirty dollars.
Twenty dollars.
Forty dollars.
Thirty-five dollars.
items.e: Twenty-five percent off forty is thirty, which is under fifty, so the extra ten dollars does not apply.

L: The fuel point is open from zero six hundred to eighteen hundred, but it shuts down for an hour at noon.
items.q: For how many hours a day can vehicles get fuel there?
o: Eleven.
Twelve.
Thirteen.
Six.
items.e: Six hundred to eighteen hundred is twelve hours, minus the one-hour break, which leaves eleven.

L: The commissary sells eggs for three dollars a dozen, but the farm stand outside the gate sells them for two fifty.
items.q: How much would someone save on four dozen eggs at the farm stand?
o: Two dollars.
Fifty cents.
Ten dollars.
Four dollars.
items.e: The farm stand is fifty cents cheaper per dozen, so four dozen saves two dollars.

L: I had hoped to get the tires for under four hundred dollars, but the cheapest set was four fifty, plus fifty for installation.
items.q: What was the total cost of the cheapest option?
o: Five hundred dollars.
Four hundred fifty dollars.
Four hundred dollars.
Five hundred fifty dollars.
items.e: Four hundred fifty for the tires plus fifty for installation comes to five hundred dollars.

L: We usually inventory the supply room once a quarter, but after last month's missing items, the captain wants it done every month.
items.q: How often will the inventory be done now?
o: Twelve times a year.
Four times a year.
Once every three months.
Twice as often as before.
items.e: Every month means twelve inventories a year instead of four.

L: Which relay are you in? I want to make sure we're not firing at the same time.
o: They put me in the last group.
I'm sure it's the same rifle.
I'll make the time if you want.
Yes, firing starts at eight.
items.e: She answers by saying she is with the final group of shooters.

L: Do you happen to know who's doing the inspection, the platoon sergeant or the commander?
o: Both of them, from what I heard.
In the hallway on the second floor.
The platoon will be ready by noon.
Yes, I happened to see him earlier.
items.e: He says that, as far as he knows, both leaders will inspect.

L: Supply ran out of my boot size. What am I supposed to wear to the field?
o: Your old pair will have to do for now.
I ran out of the field in a hurry.
Size nine, I believe.
I wore mine to the field all last year.
items.e: She tells him to keep using his old boots until new ones are available.

L: Who's supposed to be on the radio tonight while the lieutenant is at the briefing?
o: Hughes, unless he swapped again.
The briefing starts at seven tonight.
I heard it on the radio this morning.
Yes, the lieutenant will be there.
items.e: He names the soldier who should be on the radio, unless that soldier traded shifts.

L: How long is each shift on guard this weekend, two hours or four?
o: They split it into three-hour blocks.
It's about four miles long.
I shifted it to the weekend.
Two of us, plus the sergeant.
items.e: She says each shift is three hours, so neither of his guesses is right.

L: Are we supposed to bring anything to tomorrow's briefing, or do we just show up?
o: A notebook and a pen should do.
Yes, they showed up at noon.
I'll bring it up at the meeting.
Tomorrow is supposed to be rainy.
items.e: He tells her the only items she needs to bring.

L: Did you get all your shots before deploying, or do you still need some?
o: Just one more, and then I'm done.
I took a lot of photos over there.
I'm deploying sometime in May.
I still need some sleep, honestly.
items.e: She says she needs one more vaccination.

L: Is it true that you have to be back from leave a day before the field exercise?
o: That's what the company memo said.
I'll be back in a minute or two.
The field is right behind the gym.
I left a day early last time.
items.e: He confirms the rule by citing an official notice.

L: Where do I turn in these leave forms once the commander has signed them?
o: The orderly room has a box for them.
He signed them yesterday afternoon.
You can leave on Friday if you'd like.
I'll fill one out later this week.
items.e: She tells him the place to drop off the forms: a box in the orderly room.

L: Should I bring printed copies of the slides, or will everyone see them on the screen?
o: Bring some, in case the projector dies.
Yes, I brought them over yesterday afternoon.
I'll see everyone at the movie tonight.
The screen door on the porch is broken again.
items.e: He advises her to bring copies anyway, as a backup.

L: My laptop keeps shutting down in the middle of my work. Any idea what's wrong?
o: Sounds like it's overheating. Is the fan working?
I usually keep it in the middle drawer.
Sorry, I had the wrong idea about you.
Shut the door on your way out, please.
items.e: She suggests a likely cause and asks a related question.

L: We're moving to Fort Bliss next month. How do I get our mail forwarded?
o: Just file a change of address online.
I'll forward you that e-mail tonight.
We moved here about a month ago.
The mail truck usually comes around noon.
items.e: He tells her the simple step needed to have her mail sent to the new address.

L: Who's supposed to send out the minutes from yesterday's meeting? I haven't seen them.
o: That's usually Lieutenant Park's job.
It lasted about forty-five minutes.
I haven't seen him since yesterday.
I'm supposed to be out of here by noon.
items.e: She names the person who normally sends them.

L: I keep getting messages that my inbox is full. How do I clear some space?
o: Start by deleting anything with big attachments.
No thanks, I'm full. I just had a big lunch.
I got your message early this morning.
Please keep the hallway clear of boxes.
items.e: He tells her to remove the e-mails that take up the most room.

L: Who's giving the briefing to the general tomorrow, you or Captain Ruiz?
o: We're splitting it. I'll take the first half.
I gave him a birthday present yesterday.
In general, I'd say tomorrow is better.
The captain gave it to me.
items.e: She says they will share it, each giving part.

L: The neighbors upstairs play loud music every night. Is there anything housing can do?
o: Yes, once you file a written complaint.
I play the guitar every night.
The music was too loud last night.
The housing office is upstairs, on the left.
items.e: He says the office can help after she reports the problem in writing.

L: Did you remember to pack the adapters, or will we have to buy some there?
o: I packed them last night, don't worry.
We packed the whole office into one truck.
I don't remember the way there.
We'll be there for about a week.
items.e: She says she already packed the adapters, so there is no need to buy any.

L: The hotel lost our reservation. Do you want to look for another place?
o: Let's talk to the manager first.
I lost my wallet at another hotel once.
The place looks great, doesn't it?
I'm looking forward to the trip.
items.e: He would rather try to solve the problem with the manager before leaving.

L: Excuse me, which platform does the express to the city leave from?
o: The far one, just past the stairs.
It leaves every twenty minutes.
I expressed my concerns to the manager.
The city is about an hour away.
items.e: She tells him where the platform is.

L: Is this seat taken, or can I put my bag here?
o: Go ahead. Nobody's sitting there.
I took it to the shop yesterday.
I'll put the bags in the car.
I like to sit near the window.
items.e: He tells her the seat is free, so she may use it.

L: Have they started boarding yet, or do we still have time to grab a bite?
o: They just called our group, so let's go.
We grabbed a quick bite at the snack bar on base.
The board meeting started at six.
Time flies when you're having fun.
items.e: She means boarding has begun for them, so there is no time to eat.

L: Doesn't the speed limit drop to forty-five once you get into town?
o: Yes, so you'd better slow down now.
I dropped my keys in town.
There's no limit to the number of bags.
I was forty-five on my last birthday.
items.e: He confirms the lower limit and tells her to reduce her speed.

L: Which line should I get in if I've already checked in online?
o: The bag drop, over by the windows.
I usually check the news online at work.
Sure, go ahead of me.
That line was busy all day.
items.e: She tells him the right line for passengers who checked in online.

L: Did you hear the announcement? I think they said our gate was changed.
o: I missed it. Let me check the screen.
I hear they're getting married in June.
The gate was painted last week.
I changed my clothes after work.
items.e: He did not hear it, so he offers to confirm the gate on the display.

L: Would you mind if we sat out on the patio instead of near the kitchen?
o: Not at all. It's too warm in here anyway.
The kitchen closes at ten on weeknights.
I don't mind cooking for the whole family.
We sat in the back row at the movies.
items.e: She agrees to move outside, adding that it is too hot inside.

L: Should we leave a bigger tip? The waiter was really helpful with the kids.
o: Good idea. He certainly earned it.
Let's leave right after dessert.
The kids' menu is on the back.
He waited for us for twenty minutes.
items.e: He agrees that the waiter deserves a larger tip.

L: Why don't we paint the living room ourselves instead of hiring someone?
o: Fine, as long as you do the ceiling.
They're hiring at the hardware store.
Because the paint was still wet.
My room is at the end of the hall.
items.e: She accepts the suggestion on one condition.

L: What are you doing for Labor Day? We're thinking of having a barbecue.
o: Nothing so far. Is that an invitation?
We had hamburgers and corn last time.
I worked a double shift last Labor Day.
I think the grill is in the garage.
items.e: He has no plans yet and hints that he would like to be invited.

L: Would you mind feeding my cat this weekend? I'm going camping with my brother.
o: No problem. Where do you keep the food?
My brother has two cats and a dog.
We went camping there last summer.
Yes, the camp opens this weekend.
items.e: She agrees and asks where the cat food is kept.

L: Is the fish fresh today, or would you recommend something else?
o: Honestly, the chicken is better tonight.
I'd be glad to recommend you for the job.
We went fishing on the lake today.
I'll have something to drink first.
items.e: The waiter suggests the chicken, hinting that the fish is not the best choice.

L: Can I get the dressing on the side? I'm trying to cut back on calories.
o: Certainly. I'll bring it in a little cup.
I'm getting dressed right now.
I cut back on coffee last year.
The side door is locked after nine.
items.e: The server agrees to serve the dressing separately.

L: Is it all right if we bring our own birthday cake, or is there a charge?
o: Sure, but there's a small fee for that.
Sorry, my phone needs a charge right now.
We baked it ourselves this morning.
Turn right at the next light.
items.e: The restaurant allows outside cakes but charges a small fee.

L: How come you didn't get your flu shot when the clinic had walk-in hours?
o: I was running a fever that whole week.
Sure, I'll walk over there with you.
It flew by faster than I expected.
They gave me the shot in my left arm.
items.e: She explains why she missed it: she was sick with a fever at the time.

L: Why are they keeping us inside for PT this morning? It's not even raining.
o: The wind chill is way below zero.
I'll keep my raincoat inside the car.
We have PT every morning but Sunday.
I'm keeping my old boots for now.
items.e: He gives the reason: it is dangerously cold outside even without rain.

L: They're calling for thunderstorms all weekend. Do you still want to go camping at the lake?
o: Not unless the forecast changes.
I called you twice over the weekend.
The lake is about an hour north of here.
We went camping there last summer.
items.e: She means she does not want to go if the bad weather is still expected.

L: I can't make sense of my notes from today's lecture. Can I borrow yours?
o: Sure, but mine aren't much better.
It makes no sense to drive there.
I borrowed some money from my brother.
Today's lecturer was a guest speaker.
items.e: He agrees to lend his notes but warns they may not help much.

L: Did they tell you your score right away, or do you have to wait for the results?
o: It showed on the screen when I finished.
I'd rather wait in the car for you.
The score was tied at the end of the half.
They told me to turn right at the light.
items.e: She means she learned her score immediately, as soon as the test was over.

L: The line's breaking up. Can you hear me, or should I call you back on a landline?
o: Do that. You keep cutting out.
We broke up about a year ago.
The line at the bank was long.
I'll be back in an hour.
items.e: He asks her to call back because he cannot hear her clearly.

L: I'm thinking of joining the base choir. Do you think I'd fit in?
o: Why not? They're very friendly.
These shoes don't fit me anymore.
I joined right after high school.
The base is near the coast.
items.e: She encourages him, saying the choir members are welcoming.

L: Do you know if the new software will work on our old computers?
o: IT says ours are too old for it.
Yes, I know how to work it.
My old computer is in the garage.
I'll work on it after lunch.
items.e: He says the technical staff believe the computers cannot run the new program.

L: The medic said I should take these pills with food. Does that mean before or after eating?
o: During the meal is best.
I took them before I left.
The food here is pretty good.
He said it after lunch.
items.e: She explains that the pills should be taken while eating.

L: I promised my kids I'd be home Friday. Is the field exercise still ending Thursday night?
It was, until the brigade tacked on two more days of night training. Now we won't be back before Saturday evening.
items.q: What does the man's answer mean for the woman?
o: She won't be home on the day she planned.
The exercise has been cut short by two days.
Her kids can visit the training area Friday.
The brigade has canceled the night training.
items.e: The two extra days mean they return Saturday, after the Friday she promised.

L: I heard Specialist Tran didn't graduate with the rest of her class.
She hurt her wrist the week before the final exam, so they're letting her finish with the next class instead of starting over.
items.q: What can be concluded about Specialist Tran?
o: She will complete the course later.
She failed the final exam last week.
She must repeat the whole course from the start.
She has left the course for good.
items.e: She was injured and will finish with the following class without restarting.

L: We need to top off the tanks before the convoy leaves Sunday morning.
Better do it today, then. The fuel point's closed on weekends, and nobody's going to open it for us.
o: Refueling the trucks before the weekend
Leaving with the convoy on Saturday
Asking someone to open the fuel point
Waiting until Sunday morning to get fuel
items.e: Because the fuel point is closed on weekends, they must fill up now.

L: My shift on staff duty ended an hour ago, and Sergeant Ortiz still hasn't shown up to relieve me.
Don't leave the desk. Call the staff duty officer and let him track Ortiz down.
items.q: What does the woman tell the man?
o: Remain on duty and report the problem
Go looking for Sergeant Ortiz on his own
Leave now, since his shift has ended
Take over Sergeant Ortiz's next shift
items.e: She tells him not to leave and to let the staff duty officer locate his relief.

L: Why did all those cars pull over a minute ago? There's no accident.
It's five o'clock. When the bugle plays for the flag coming down, everyone on post stops and pays respect.
o: A daily ceremony was taking place.
An accident had blocked the road.
The gate closes at five o'clock.
A parade was coming down the street.
items.e: Traffic stops at five when the flag is lowered to music, out of respect.

L: Did Sergeant Boyd really weigh everyone's ruck before we stepped off?
Every single one. Mine was three pounds light, so he made me carry two extra cans of water.
items.q: Why did the woman have to carry more?
o: Her pack didn't meet the minimum.
She had forgotten to bring her water.
Her ruck was too heavy.
Sergeant Boyd asked her to help him.
items.e: Her ruck was three pounds too light, so extra weight was added.

L: On my last round I found the back door of the barracks propped open with a rock.
Somebody probably got tired of using the main entrance. Secure it, write down the time, and check it again next round.
items.q: What is the woman told to do?
o: Lock it and make a note in the log
Find out who left the door open
Use the main entrance from now on
Report the problem to the first sergeant
items.e: He tells her to secure the door, record the time, and check it on her next round.

L: I'm applying for the warrant officer program. Do you think the colonel would write me a letter of recommendation?
He might, but he barely knows you. Your company commander's letter would carry more weight.
o: Asking someone more familiar with him
Not applying for the program this year
Writing the letter himself
Getting letters from both officers
items.e: She thinks a letter from his own commander, who knows him better, would be stronger.

L: My ID card expires on the thirtieth. Can I just walk in at the ID office?
You can try, but the wait is usually three or four hours. Most people book online.
o: Scheduling ahead would save her time.
Her card expired a few days ago.
The office closes early on the thirtieth.
She can renew her card entirely online.
items.e: Walk-ins wait for hours, so booking an appointment online is the faster way.

L: Why is your computer showing that blue screen? Did it crash?
No, it's just installing updates. It started on its own, and it says it'll take another forty minutes.
items.q: What can be concluded about the woman?
o: Her computer is unavailable for now.
She has to replace her computer.
She started the updates herself.
Her computer crashed forty minutes ago.
items.e: The updates will take forty more minutes, so she cannot use the computer until then.

L: I tried calling Major Hill all morning, but his voicemail is full.
He's at a conference in Denver all week. You'd have better luck sending him an email.
items.q: Why does the man suggest email?
o: The major is away from the office.
The major's phone is broken.
The major prefers written messages.
The conference ends this morning.
items.e: Major Hill is at a conference in Denver for the whole week.

L: Where can I get this power of attorney notarized before I deploy?
The legal office does it for free, but only on Tuesday and Thursday mornings. Bring your ID.
items.q: What does the woman say about the service?
o: It is free but not available daily.
It is available only after deployment.
It requires an appointment on Tuesday.
It is offered every morning.
items.e: It costs nothing, but it is offered only two mornings a week.

L: Are you still living in the barracks?
Not since my promotion. I share an apartment in town with two guys from my section now.
items.q: What can be concluded about the man?
o: He no longer lives on base.
He lives alone in town.
He was recently demoted.
He moved into the barracks.
items.e: After his promotion he moved to an apartment in town.

L: The fifteenth is a Sunday this month. Does that mean we don't get paid until Monday?
Just the opposite. When payday lands on a weekend, the money comes on the Friday before.
o: On the thirteenth
On the fifteenth
On the sixteenth
On the seventeenth
items.e: The fifteenth is a Sunday, so the Friday before it is the thirteenth.

L: When do we get the clothing allowance? My boots are falling apart.
Once a year, on the anniversary of the month you came in. For you, that's not until August.
items.q: What can be concluded about the woman?
o: She will not be paid for a while yet.
She joined the service in January.
She received the money in August.
Her boots were replaced last year.
items.e: Her allowance is not paid until August.

L: Do I need to bring anything to the quarterly training brief?
Your training calendar, and a printed copy of the range requests. The commander doesn't want laptops in the room.
o: He should bring paper, not a computer.
The commander will bring the calendar.
The brief has been moved to the range.
Laptops will be provided in the room.
items.e: Laptops are not allowed, so he must bring printed documents.

L: Hey, the spreadsheet you sent won't open on my computer.
You must have the older version of the program. I'll save it in a different format and resend it.
items.q: What will the man probably do next?
o: Send her a converted copy
Update the program for her
Give her his computer
Make a new spreadsheet
items.e: He will save the file in another format and send it again.

L: Any chance of getting on the space-available flight to Ramstein tonight?
There are eight seats, but you're number twenty on the list, so I wouldn't count on it.
o: He is very unlikely to get on that flight.
Only eight people signed up for the flight.
The flight to Ramstein leaves at eight.
He is next on the waiting list.
items.e: Nineteen people are ahead of him for only eight seats, so he is unlikely to fly.

L: Does the number seven bus still stop in front of the library?
Not this month. With the road work on Main, it's been moved two blocks over, to Elm.
items.q: What does the man say about the bus?
o: For now, it runs on another street.
It no longer runs on weekdays.
It stops at the library twice an hour.
It has been replaced by the number two.
items.e: Because of road work on Main Street, the bus uses Elm Street this month.

L: Do I have to fill up the rental before I bring it back tomorrow?
You don't have to, but if they fill it for you, it's almost nine dollars a gallon.
o: Refueling it himself would be cheaper.
The car must be returned today.
The gas station is nine miles away.
The rental already has a full tank.
items.e: The rental company charges a very high price for fuel, so filling it himself saves money.

L: Will my state driver's license be enough to drive in Korea once I get there?
Not by itself. You'll also have to pass a short written test on base before they'll give you a local permit.
items.q: What does the man say about the woman's license?
o: It won't be enough on its own.
It must be renewed before she leaves.
It will be exchanged at the airport.
It is good for her whole tour.
items.e: He says her license is not enough by itself; she must also pass a test on base for a local permit.

L: My phone says the hotel is right here, but this is an empty parking lot.
Your map must be out of date. The hotel moved downtown last year. I'll call for the new address.
o: The phone's information is old.
The hotel parking lot is full.
The hotel closed down last year.
The phone battery has died.
items.e: The map on the phone still shows the hotel's former location.

L: Could I get a wake-up call at four fifteen, please?
Certainly. The breakfast room won't be open that early, so I'll have a breakfast bag waiting for you at the desk.
o: Food she can take with her
An early breakfast at four fifteen
A ride to catch the first flight
A later wake-up call at six
items.e: Breakfast will not be served yet, so he will prepare a breakfast bag for her.

L: The estimate came back at fourteen thousand pounds, and my allowance is only twelve thousand.
Then it's time for a yard sale. Otherwise, the extra weight comes out of your own pocket.
o: Getting rid of some belongings
Asking for a higher estimate
Buying more at a yard sale
Paying for a bigger moving truck
items.e: She advises selling things so he does not have to pay for the extra weight.

L: I'm dropping my car off at the shipping center tomorrow. I'll fill up the tank on the way.
Don't. They won't accept it with more than a quarter tank of gas.
o: She shouldn't add fuel to the car.
The shipping center sells cheap gas.
She has to fill a quarter of the tank.
The car must be dropped off today.
items.e: The center refuses cars with too much gas, so she should not fill the tank.

L: Is the ferry to the island still running this afternoon?
They canceled the two o'clock because of high winds, and the four o'clock doesn't look any better.
o: The later boat may not sail either.
The ferry leaves at two o'clock.
The wind has finally calmed down.
The four o'clock is sold out.
items.e: The wind is still strong, so the four o'clock may also be canceled.

L: I dropped off my prescription at the pharmacy an hour ago. Is it ready yet?
Let me check. It looks like we're waiting on your doctor to approve the dose. Could you come back after lunch?
o: It needs the doctor's approval first.
The pharmacy is closed for lunch.
She dropped it off at the wrong place.
The medicine is out of stock.
items.e: The pharmacy is waiting for her doctor to approve the dose.

L: Did the clinic call you back about your blood test?
They did. Everything came back normal, but they want me to cut down on salt and come back in six months.
items.q: What can be concluded about the woman?
o: She does not have a serious problem.
She must return to the clinic next month.
She needs another blood test today.
She has stopped eating salt completely.
items.e: Her results were normal; she only needs to eat less salt and have a routine follow-up.

L: My orders to Korea came through. Do I need any shots before I go?
Probably a few. Take your shot record to immunizations; they'll compare it with the requirements for that region.
items.q: What should the woman do first?
o: Have her vaccine records checked
Get every shot before receiving orders
Ask her unit about travel to Korea
Request a copy of her new orders
items.e: The immunization clinic will compare her record with what is required for Korea.

L: Personnel says I can't start the leadership course next month. Something about my medical readiness being red.
That usually means your annual health assessment is overdue. Book it today, and you should be cleared in time.
items.q: Why can't the man attend the course yet?
o: A yearly medical exam is overdue.
He failed the course entrance test.
The course is full until next month.
His leader has not approved it.
items.e: The woman explains that his annual health check is late, which blocks him from the course.

L: I've been throwing up since midnight. Should I still come in for the inventory today?
Absolutely not. The last thing we need is the whole section catching it. Stay home, keep drinking fluids, and I'll cover for you.
items.q: Why does the man want the woman to stay home?
o: To keep others from getting sick
So that she can finish the inventory
Because the section is closed today
So that she can see a doctor
items.e: He does not want her illness to spread to the rest of the section.

L: My shins have been aching after every run this month.
How old are your running shoes? Once they've got a few hundred miles on them, the cushioning is gone, and your legs take the beating.
items.q: What does the woman think the problem is?
o: His shoes no longer absorb impact.
He has been running too few miles.
He bought shoes that are too small.
His legs are not getting enough rest.
items.e: She thinks his shoes are worn out and no longer cushion his legs.

L: That coffee line is out the door. We'll never make the eight o'clock briefing.
Watch this. I'll order on the app, and it'll be waiting on the pickup counter before we even get inside.
items.q: What does the man plan to do?
o: Place their order using his phone
Skip coffee to make the briefing
Wait in line until eight o'clock
Go to a different coffee shop
items.e: He will order ahead with the app so the coffee is ready when they arrive.

L: My windshield's covered in ice, and I'm already late. Can I just pour hot water on it?
Don't. The sudden temperature change can crack the glass. Start the engine, run the defroster, and use a scraper.
items.q: What does the woman warn the man about?
o: The windshield could be damaged.
He will be late if he waits.
Hot water will freeze on the road.
The defroster might not work.
items.e: She says hot water on icy glass can make it crack.

L: Are you taking the kids to the base pool this afternoon like you promised?
I was planning to, but have you looked outside? Those clouds are getting darker by the minute.
o: The outing may be canceled because of the weather.
The kids have already gone to the pool without him.
He promised to clean the pool this afternoon.
He would rather go to the pool in the morning.
items.e: Darkening clouds suggest a storm, so the trip to the pool may not happen.

L: My car insurance is going up again, even though I haven't had a single accident.
Have you shopped around? When I compared rates last spring, I ended up saving almost three hundred a year.
o: Checking prices at other companies
Waiting until spring to renew
Asking about accident records in his area
Paying the yearly rate all at once
items.e: She saved money by comparing rates, so she suggests he look at other insurers.

L: I'm thinking about getting one of those warehouse club memberships. Is it worth the sixty dollars?
Only if you have the space. We bought forty rolls of paper towels, and they're still in our hallway.
o: Bulk buying requires a lot of storage.
The membership costs too much for most people.
His family uses paper towels very quickly.
The warehouse club is in his neighborhood.
items.e: He bought so much that it still fills his hallway, so you need room to store large purchases.

L: The guy upstairs is moving furniture again at midnight. This is the third time this week.
Have you actually talked to him about it? He might not realize how much noise carries.
o: Discussing the matter with the neighbor
Moving to an apartment upstairs
Calling the police at midnight
Helping him move his furniture
items.e: She thinks the neighbor may not know he is loud, so the man should speak to him.

L: I need to open a checking account for my daughter. She just started her first job.
If she's under eighteen, you'll have to come in with her and sign as a joint owner.
items.q: What does the man say about the account?
o: A parent might need to share it.
Only adults can open a checking account.
The daughter must open it by herself.
Her employer must sign the forms.
items.e: A minor needs a parent to sign as a joint owner of the account.

L: My sister's getting married in Hawaii, and the whole family is invited.
Lucky you! But a wedding in Hawaii must cost guests a fortune. Are you actually going?
items.q: What is the woman concerned about?
o: The price of attending the event
The size of the man's family
The weather in Hawaii that week
The date that his sister picked for the wedding
items.e: She thinks traveling to a wedding in Hawaii is very expensive for guests.

L: I finally found a house to rent, but the owner wants first and last month's rent plus a deposit.
Ouch. That's three months' worth of money up front. Can you swing it?
o: Whether she can afford the payment
Whether she will move into the house
Whether the owner lives nearby
Whether she will rent for three months
items.e: Can you swing it means: do you have enough money for it?

L: Mom called. She's wondering if we can host the family reunion this summer.
In this little house? We'd have people sleeping in the bathtub. Maybe we could rent a cabin instead.
o: Their home doesn't have enough room.
Renting a cabin costs too much money.
Summer is a busy time for the family.
She doesn't get along with his mother.
items.e: Their house is too small for all the relatives.

L: Did you remember to pick up Lily from daycare? They close at six.
Oh no, I thought it was your turn today. It's five fifty. I can make it if I leave right now.
items.q: What will the man probably do next?
o: Hurry to get their daughter
Call the daycare to say he's late
Wait for his wife to go
Pick up Lily tomorrow
items.e: He has only ten minutes, so he will leave at once.

L: I've been teaching myself guitar from online videos, but my fingers still hurt after ten minutes.
That makes two of us. I gave up on the violin after a month for the same reason.
o: She had a similar problem with an instrument.
She and the man take guitar lessons together.
She can teach him to play the violin.
She practices for ten minutes every day.
items.e: "That makes two of us" means "me too": her fingers also hurt, and she quit the violin.

L: My instructor keeps telling me I pronounce "ship" and "sheep" exactly the same way.
Record yourself reading the word list, then compare it with the audio. That helped me with my "th" sound.
o: Listening to her own voice for differences
Asking the instructor for a new list
Practicing the "th" sound every day
Avoiding words that sound alike
items.e: He suggests she tape her own speech and compare it with the model recording.

L: I'm stuck in traffic outside the gate. Go ahead and start the movie without me.
We'll wait. The previews take twenty minutes anyway, so you'll probably make it.
o: He will likely get there in time.
They should start the film without him.
The traffic will last twenty minutes.
He ought to see a later show.
items.e: Because the previews are long, she expects him to arrive before the film begins.

L: Your tomatoes are huge this year. What's your secret?
No secret. I just moved the garden to the other side of the house, where it gets sun all afternoon.
o: The location of his plants
The kind of tomatoes he grows
The time of day he waters
The size of his house
items.e: He put the garden in a sunnier spot.

L: Want to shoot some pool after dinner?
I'd love to, but I really need to hit the books. My final is the day after tomorrow.
items.q: What will the woman probably do this evening?
o: Study for an upcoming exam
Play pool with the man
Return some library books
Take her final exam
items.e: "Hit the books" means study; her exam is in two days.

L: I've practiced Spanish on my phone app for two hundred days in a row.
Impressive! I usually give up on those things after a week.
items.q: What can be inferred about the man?
o: He has trouble sticking with study apps.
He has studied Spanish for two hundred days.
He uses the app once a week.
He doesn't own a smartphone.
items.e: He admits he stops using such apps quickly.

L: The bookstore wants ninety dollars for the new edition of our grammar book.
The instructor said the old edition is fine. You can find used copies for around fifteen.
o: The man can save money on his book.
The new edition is required for class.
Used copies cost ninety dollars.
The instructor wrote the grammar book.
items.e: An older, used copy is acceptable and costs much less.

L: Every time I log in to my email, it sends a code to my phone. It's so annoying.
It's a pain, but it stops strangers from getting into your account even if they learn your password.
o: The extra step is worth the trouble.
The codes aren't really necessary.
Her password has already been stolen.
She should stop using her phone.
items.e: He admits it is annoying, but it protects her account, so it is worth it.

L: What should I wear to the unit ball? I've never been to one.
Your dress uniform. And be ready for a long night; they usually go past midnight.
items.q: What does the woman tell the man?
o: The event will probably end late.
He can wear whatever clothes he likes.
The ball starts at midnight.
She has never attended one.
items.e: She warns him that the ball usually lasts until after midnight.

L: The car makes a loud squeaking noise every time I brake. Should I be worried?
o: The pads are probably worn. I'd get it checked.
Take a break every couple of hours on long road trips.
It broke down on the highway last month.
The neighbors made a lot of noise last night.
items.e: She explains the probable cause of the noise and advises having the brakes inspected.

L: The kitchen faucet's been dripping for days. Do you think we can fix it ourselves?
o: It might just need a new washer. Let's look.
We cooked dinner ourselves last night, remember?
It's been raining for almost a week now.
Yes, they'll be here in a couple of days.
items.e: He thinks the repair is simple and suggests they examine the faucet together.

L: Are you coming over to watch the game Sunday, or do you have duty?
o: I'm on call, but I'll come by if it's quiet.
We watched it at my brother's place last year.
The game was rained out last Sunday.
My watch has been running slow all week.
items.e: She is on call but will visit if she is not needed at work.

L: During my walk-through, I noticed the fire extinguisher tags on the second floor are all from last year.
Then they're past due for inspection. Put in a work order with the fire department before the inspectors catch it.
o: The extinguishers are overdue for a check.
A fire started on the second floor.
The inspectors found missing extinguishers.
The fire department lost the work order.
items.e: The tags show the last inspection was a year ago, so a new one is overdue.

L: The food drive was supposed to end Friday, but people keep bringing in cans.
Then let's leave the boxes in the lobby through next week. The shelter can always use more.
o: Extending the collection period
Closing the food drive on Friday
Moving the boxes out of the lobby
Asking the shelter for more cans
items.e: He wants to keep collecting donations for another week.

L: Supply says the brake pads for our trucks are on back order until March.
March? We can't keep half the fleet off the road that long. Check whether the depot in Texas has any.
items.q: What does the woman want the man to do?
o: Find the parts somewhere else
Wait for the parts until March
Drive the trucks to Texas
Order new trucks for the fleet
items.e: She can't wait until March, so she wants him to see if a depot in Texas has the pads.

L: For the unit bake sale, I'm making three dozen brownies. What are you bringing?
Honestly, I can't bake to save my life. How about I run the cash box instead?
items.q: What does the man offer to do?
o: Handle the money at the sale
Bake three dozen brownies
Buy cookies at the store
Teach the woman how to bake
items.e: He can't bake, so he offers to take care of the cash box.

L: This TV is three hundred dollars cheaper at the store across town.
Bring up their ad on your phone. We match any local competitor's price.
Great, that saves me a trip.
o: A salesclerk in the store
A friend who owns a TV
A manager from across town
A repair technician
items.e: She speaks for the store ('we match'), so she must work there.

L: Gas is almost forty cents a gallon cheaper across the state line. Should we fill up there?
It's a thirty-mile drive each way. Whatever we'd save, we'd burn getting there.
o: The trip would cancel out any savings.
Gas is cheaper in their own state.
They should drive over there now.
Their tank is too small to fill up.
items.e: Driving sixty miles round trip would use up the money they'd save.
